Plus discounts on merchandise etc.  So when people ask me about Dividend traps my answer is always, depends..?

@paulthoded @e2e4au and @Retiredmco's comments likely referred to the fact that in a Ponzi scheme the payments to investors are not earned, but paid out of substance. They are return of capital, so to speak. However, a Ponzi scheme is uniquely different from these ETFs in that the capital, from which the returns are paid, are generally new investor money. Late investors pay earlier ones, until the scheme runs out of new recruits. That's not the case here. The result here is simply net asset erosion. In an up-market, the 1.5x amplifier may pay returns while maintaining NAV. Unfortunately, with the 1.5x amplifier, in a down market erosion can occur very quickly. @paulthoded @e2e4au and @Retiredmco's comments likely referred to the fact that in a Ponzi scheme the payments to investors are not earned, but paid out of substance. They are return of capital, so to speak. However, a Ponzi scheme is uniquely different from these ETFs in that the capital, from which the returns are paid, are generally new investor money. Late investors pay earlier ones, until the scheme runs out of new recruits. That's not the case here. The result here is simply net asset erosion. In an up-market, the 1.5x amplifier may pay returns while maintaining NAV. Unfortunately, with the 1.5x amplifier, in a down market erosion can occur very quickly.
